name: refraction-by-age
label: Mean refraction trajectories by age: the J0 slope (a calibration target) and spherical-equivalent changes (for comparison)

sources.citation: Study of age-related corneal geometry and astigmatism (PMC6221551; search excerpt, 2026-10-29): 'the mean values of J0 and corneal J0 decreased by -0.014 and -0.015 per year of increase in age, indicating astigmatic shift toward ATR', correlated with horizontal steepening and vertical flattening of the cornea. The age range is not in the excerpt; 30-80 is an assumption.
sources.seCitation: assumption: no standard error in the excerpt; 0.003 D/yr spans this and the Hong Kong estimate.

sources.citation: Hong Kong clinical study (The Hong Kong Polytechnic University, ira.lib.polyu.edu.hk handle 10397/25994; search excerpt, 2026-10-29): refractive and corneal J0 fell synchronously, -0.15 and -0.14 D per 10 years, after the age of 30; the population moved from mostly WTR to ATR with age. The upper age is not in the excerpt (assumption).

Beesley & Elliott 2024 (doi 10.1111/opo.13234; search excerpt): 640 eyes followed a median of 20 years from mean age 46; most cylinder changes came after the mid-40s; increases of ATR changed faster per decade than the earlier decreases of WTR (0.71 vs 0.34 D per decade; whether clinical cylinder or J0 is not in the excerpt).
sources.useNote: Rates in eyes that changed, not population means; kept for comparison with the model's individual trajectories.

sources.citation: Six-year changes in refraction and related ocular biometric factors in an adult Chinese population (Guangzhou; search excerpt, 2026-10-29): mean spherical-equivalent changes +0.24, +0.51, +0.26, and -0.05 D for baseline ages 35-44, 45-54, 55-64, and 65+; a hyperopic shift before 65 and a myopic shift after.
sources.useNote: Adult spherical-equivalent changes are dominated by the crystalline lens (hyperopic shift, then nuclear myopia), which the mechanical model does not contain; fitting them would push the homeostatic ratio to stand in for the lens (M5 plan, Task 5.9 notes). Kept for comparison.
sources.boundNote: The bounding fit (M5 plan, Task 5.14 Step 6; `eyebiomech calibrate --bound-sphere`) requires only that the mechanical six-year change of the mean spherical equivalent in each band not exceed the observed change in magnitude: the lens, not modeled, accounts for the rest, so the observed change is an envelope, not a target.
sources.boundSeCitation: assumption: no standard error in the excerpt; 0.1 D, about a third of the largest band change, so a mechanical change one band-change beyond the envelope costs a few units of chi-square.

sources.citation: Prevalence of refractive error in the United States, 1999-2004 (NHANES autorefraction; PMC2772054; search excerpt, 2026-10-29; authors not in the excerpt): age-standardized prevalence in adults 20 and older of hyperopia 3.6%, myopia 33.1%, astigmatism 36.2%; age-by-refraction distributions only as figures. The raw VIX files can be downloaded with eyebiomech.calib.download_nhanes (cdc.gov was unreachable from the cloud session).
